item.title: Shapiro Accuses Biden of Not Doing Enough to Rein In Netanyahu
item.description: The Pennsylvania governor said Biden didn’t go far enough to constrain Netanyahu in his first interview on foreign policy ahead of a potential 2028 run.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis Take Second Swipe at Tallest Tower in Saudi Capital
item.description: The strike on the Public Investment Fund Tower follows a previous Houthi assault on the building on Thursday.

item.title: China’s Huawei Convicted of Fraud in U.S. Criminal Trial
item.description: A federal jury convicted the tech and telecom giant of fraud and other offenses but acquitted it of racketeering conspiracy.

item.title: Venezuela Reveals an Eye-Popping Debt Load of $237 Billion
item.description: The higher-than-expected figure underscores the challenges faced by the U.S.-backed interim government.

item.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Shipping Risks Persist
item.description: Oil prices picked up from initial losses and settled higher Tuesday as traders weighed persistent threats to energy shipments in the Middle East against expectations of a global supply surplus.

item.description: The Nvidia co-founder thanked the Trump administration while addressing staff the day after he was reinstated as CEO.

item.title: I Went Inside Chornobyl as Ukraine Races to Secure It
item.description: Watch how Ukrainian engineers and the armed forces are racing to contain radiation at the nuclear power plant.

item.title: China Takes Down Shanghai Party Boss Once Seen as Potential Leader
item.description: Chen Jining, the party secretary of Shanghai, has been placed under investigation on suspicion of severe violations of party discipline and state laws.

item.title: British Police Arrest Two Men Over Suspected Burglary at Royal Estate
item.description: The police searched the estate where Prince William and Kate have a country home.

item.title: China to Suspend Some Critical-Material Export Curbs to U.S. Until January
